extracted.intended_audience: academics and researchers (especially Loughborough University staff and researchers) who review or publish research
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and practical guidance on open peer review: definitions of open peer review elements and types, pros and cons of openness, journals/platforms using OPR, and ways researchers can make their review activity visible and get credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Author and reviewer identities are disclosed (to each other, and to the reader).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one element of Open Peer Review (per Ross-Hellauer, 2017). Openness of identities increases transparency but may influence reviewer behaviour and willingness to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The review reports are published alongside the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing review reports makes the content of peer review visible to readers and can be used for training and accountability; it is one of the dimensions that can be combined to create different OPR models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The wider community can contribute to the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR implementations can allow non-invited community members to comment or review, expanding who can evaluate the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct discussions between authors, editors and reviewers are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR can facilitate direct dialogues (rather than asynchronous hidden reports), which may clarify criticisms and foster constructive revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint open peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of preprints (e.g. on preprint servers) is possible before formal peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprint review allows feedback prior to journal submission and can operate independently of formal journal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers can comment; and authors/other readers respond post-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR may include mechanisms for ongoing discourse after publication, enabling continued critique and correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open platforms (decoupled review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is facilitated by a different organisational entity than the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also called 'decoupled review'; platforms or third parties can coordinate peer review separate from where the article is ultimately published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of peer review (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different peer-review models exist: single-blind, double-blind, signed, collaborative, portable, published, post-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: Single-blind (reviewers know authors, reviewers anonymous), Double-blind (both identities protected), Signed (reviewers sign comments; authors receive names), Collaborative (reviewers collaborate or confer with authors/editors), Portable (reviewers shared across journals/organisations), Published (reviewer comments and/or names published), Post-publication (community reviews after posting; reviewer names usually published).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and accountability (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Increased transparency and accountability: since the process is transparent, reviewers are held to account for their report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency can help prevent citation manipulation, conflicts of interest and reduce bias; listed as a pro of OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive criticism (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing the author’s name is likely to push reviewers to write a more balanced review where strengths as well as weaknesses are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR may encourage reviewers to provide constructive, balanced feedback rather than overly harsh or cursory comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open debate (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Open identities and reviews facilitate debate whereby readers can see the reviewers’ comments and the author’s responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables transparent scholarly discourse and debate in the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training opportunity (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: When review reports are published, they can be used as learning opportunities for early career researchers who may be inexperienced in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published reports serve as exemplars for good reviews and can support reviewer training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive for credit (benefit)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPR gives reviewers recognition for their role by making review activities visible and citable by assigning DOIs to reviews which can be used in ORCID profiles and cited in CVs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible reviews can be integrated into researcher profiles and used as demonstrable service/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced scholarly rigour (risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are fears that OPR may lead to a decrease in scholarly rigour if reviewers temper their criticisms for fear of reprisals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a con of open peer review: openness might cause reviewers to soften critiques, potentially lowering review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential bias (risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may write more positive reviews for researchers who are well-established in their fields or for papers which focus on perceived ‘hot’ topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR can accentuate social biases; openness of identity may advantage high-status authors or fashionable topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arduous review process (cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: While the quality of review may improve, as the review is open to more scrutiny, reviewers may spend significantly longer reviewing papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time burden on reviewers could increase under OPR, affecting reviewer availability and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of open identities (practical constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some scholars may refuse to review papers if their names are to be revealed, potentially reducing the pool of reviewers for some journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPR policies that require identity disclosure may lead to reviewer attrition, especially in small or contentious fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload review report to institutional Research Repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload an open peer review report as an output directly to the Research Repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This will appear in LUPIN alongside other outputs and also be made available externally; a mechanism for making reviews public when publisher does not provide OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add peer review activities to LUPIN Professional Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Add your peer review activities to your LUPIN profile, under Professional Activities (journals, publishers, funders reviewed for and frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently internal visibility but there are plans to optionally surface this content on individual staff web pages; useful for recording service.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID — trusted organisation uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a 'trusted organisation' upload review activity to ORCID for reviewers who disclose their ORCID ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One way to automatically make reviews visible on your ORCID record when the publisher/platform supports it.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID — add reviews under Professional Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually add your peer review activities under Professional Activities as a form of Service on ORCID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative manual method to record review work if automatic upload is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarivate (Web of Science) Researcher Profile — automatic addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a free Researcher Profile with Clarivate and review for an organisation with a Clarivate Agreement so your review activity (not the content) will be automatically added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic inclusion shows service activity on your Clarivate profile when agreements exist between publisher/organisations and Clarivate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarivate Researcher Profile — manual addition
rubrics_metrics.description: Manually add your peer review activity to your Clarivate Researcher Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If automatic transfer is not available, you can still record review activity on Clarivate profiles manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher reviewer recognition opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual publishers may offer recognition and reward schemes for reviewers (examples: Elsevier Reviewer Recognition Platform; Taylor & Francis; other publisher schemes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a publisher does not offer OPR, ask whether they have mechanisms to make your review available or recognise reviewer contributions; some publishers provide DOIs or other credit systems.
